input.comfortZone: comfortable texting but terrified of phone calls

output.acknowledgment: You have texting as a real strength, and you want to use reconnecting with old friends as the direction to stretch toward phone calls.
output.if_you_dont: Noticing which option felt most or least appealing still tells you something useful about where your edge actually sits.

pushes.label: Warm-Up Text First
pushes.challenge: Text one old friend a short, genuine message - something like 'been thinking about you lately' - and at the end add a line offering to catch up by phone if they ever want to. You do not have to initiate the call; you are just leaving the door open in writing first.
pushes.time_frame: Today or this weekend, whenever you have ten quiet minutes to compose it.
pushes.why_this_size: It stays inside texting, which is comfortable, while nudging one inch toward phone territory. The offer is optional and low-pressure for both of you.
pushes.what_counts: Sending the text with the phone-call offer included. Their reply, or lack of one, is not part of what counts.
pushes.if_too_much: Send the warm message without the phone offer. Just reopening contact counts.

pushes.label: Leave a Voicemail
pushes.challenge: Call an old friend at a time you reasonably expect they will not pick up - maybe mid-morning on a workday - and leave a short voicemail. Thirty seconds is enough: your name, that you were thinking of them, and that no reply is needed if life is busy. Scripting it in advance on paper is fine.
pushes.time_frame: Pick a specific 10-minute window in the next two days and block it now.
pushes.why_this_size: A voicemail uses your voice and the phone without requiring a live, two-way conversation. It is a real step past texting, but the open-ended unpredictability of a real-time call is not there.
pushes.what_counts: Dialing the number and leaving any voicemail, however short.
pushes.if_too_much: Write out what you would say as if it were a voicemail script, without actually calling. Seeing the words in your voice is still useful information.

pushes.label: Capped Live Call
pushes.challenge: Text a friend first to set it up: ask if they are free for a quick 10-minute call at a specific time you name. The cap is built into the invitation, so you are not committing to an open-ended conversation. When the time comes, dial in.
pushes.time_frame: Send the scheduling text today; plan the call for sometime in the next three to five days.
pushes.why_this_size: Scheduling it in advance removes the cold-start anxiety of calling unannounced, and the 10-minute limit keeps the call from feeling bottomless. The texting step first lets you enter phone territory from familiar ground.
pushes.what_counts: Sending the scheduling text with a specific time proposed. If they agree and the call happens, that is a bonus - but the text itself is the controllable attempt.
pushes.if_too_much: Send the scheduling text but name a time a week out, giving yourself more runway before the call actually arrives.
